extracted.intended_audience: essay contest judges and volunteer scorers (K-12/student contests)
extracted.subtask_description: Scoring and evaluating student essays submitted to a writing contest using a 1–5 scale across several dimensions (understanding, originality, point-of-view, and literary mechanics). Intended for volunteer judges or teachers completing one form per essay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring instructions / scale
rubrics_metrics.description: For each criterion listed, score the essay on a scale of 1-5, with 5 being the best score. Use a separate form for each essay. Do not score in decimals or fractions – whole numbers only. 1=Poor/Incomplete, 2=Below Average, 3=Average, 4=Above Average, 5=Excellent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score each criterion using whole numbers only (no decimals). Complete a separate rubric form per essay. The numeric labels correspond to qualitative categories: 5 (Excellent), 4 (Above average), 3 (Average), 2 (Below average), 1 (Poor/Incomplete). Total the criterion scores to compute the Total Score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding of the topic
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent did the writer demonstrate a clear understanding of the question and respond with details about his/her experience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
5 — Excellent / In-depth understanding: key concepts related to the question and the story are identified and fully defined; excellent use of literary techniques such as comparison and contrast.
4 — Above average: Key concepts related to the question and the story are adequately identified and defined; average use of literary techniques to describe viewpoints.
3 — Average: Key concepts are partially identified and defined; statement that viewpoints exist but little use of supporting details.
2 — Below average: Some concepts are identified but not defined; lack of reference to any viewpoints.
1 — Poor: Complete lack of reference to the question and the story; irrelevant information; unsupported statements; incomplete details.
(Also presented in table language: Fully, relative to the topic; Mostly relative to the topic without errors; Partially relative with minor errors; Somewhat relative with significant errors; Not relative to the topic at all.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Original thinking relative to the topic
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent was the original thinking relative to the subject?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the originality and freshness of ideas and insights related to the topic. (The rubric presents this as a 1–5 scale where 5 is 'Excellent' and 1 is 'Poor'; specific level descriptors are aligned with the general 5–1 scale used across criteria.) Evaluate whether the essay demonstrates unique perspective, creative interpretation, or novel connections to the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness in presenting a point-of-view
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent did the writer present his/her point of view?
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
5 — Point-of-view fully presented and supported by many facts.
4 — Point-of-view presented and supported with some facts.
3 — Point-of-view expressed but limited use of factual information.
2 — Point-of-view presented without use of supporting facts / opinion only.
1 — Facts are inaccurate / Point of view not present.
(Assess clarity, strength, and factual support of the essay's central stance.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary style, grammar and spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the essay's literary style along with grammar and spelling correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
5 — Literary style completely clear and effective, excellent grammar and spelling; varied sentence structure, essay well developed and cohesive.
4 — Literary style partially clear and effective, good grammar & spelling; sentence structure somewhat varied; essay well developed and cohesive.
3 — Use of literary technique to convey main ideas but lacking clarity; sentence structure lacks variety but essay mostly developed.
2 — Lacks use of literary technique; many errors in grammar and spelling.
1 — Irrelevant and/or erroneous information, main ideas unclear, illegible; grammar and spelling errors consistent throughout essay.
(Assess voice, clarity, sentence variety, organization/cohesion, and mechanical correctness.)
